principles: Bots NEVER bind to personal accounts. Period. No exceptions.
Each bot identity must be on a dedicated SIM, dedicated email, dedicated Discord/Slack workspace.
Identity binding requires written rationale + 7-day cooling-off review before going live.
Auto-reply to non-allowlisted DMs defaults to silent_ignore — NEVER emit pairing codes, verification codes, or any token to a human without explicit per-message approval.

If a bot's bound identity is permanently entangled with personal identity (phone-number-based channels like WhatsApp/iMessage), the channel is permanently disqualified for bot use until the entanglement is broken (separate SIM / separate Apple ID).

personal_identities_quarantined._comment: These identifiers belong to the human operator. NO agent may bind to or send AS these.

marline_telegram.notes: Channel currently disabled; re-enable gated by containment-register entry.

kira_telegram.notes: Channel currently disabled; env-hydration wrapper rebuild required first.

asterix_discord.notes: Single-claim guarded after Cursor MCP hijack. See namespace-ownership.policy.json for outbound-scan ban.

deny_bind.reason: WhatsApp identity is phone-number-bound; impossible to separate from personal identity without a dedicated SIM. Apr 28 2026 incident: bot attached to +972549961347 with dmPolicy=allowlist auto-replied with pairing codes (PTUKVDSL, ERYXT5QX) to two real human contacts (Chana Flam, Herschel) who looked like phishing.
deny_bind.lifted_when: Dedicated SIM acquired AND new WhatsApp account registered to that SIM AND verified that all personal contacts have been notified the new number is a bot.

deny_bind.reason: iMessage identity is Apple-ID-bound. Same risk shape as WhatsApp.
deny_bind.lifted_when: Dedicated Apple ID created AND verified separate from personal Apple ID's iCloud / Find My / Photos / etc.

auto_reply_defaults._comment: OpenClaw's pairing flow was the proximate cause of the Apr 28 incident. Default behavior must be to drop unknown-sender messages, not auto-respond.

ask_before_emitting._comment: Any message matching these rules, sent to a recipient classified as 'human_identity' (not a bot_identities_allowed entry), requires per-message approval — even for the publisher role. The PreToolUse channel-identity-check hook (P3) consumes this directly: each rule is machine-enforceable, no prose-described regex.

_schema.id: stable identifier — used in audit logs and ack-tracking
_schema.pattern: for keyword: case-insensitive substring of message body; for regex: a real regex matched against the full message body; for message_shape: a structured shape descriptor (currently supports 'standalone_short_alphanum')
_schema.applies_to: recipient classification — currently always 'human_identity', but reserved for future 'bot_identity' / 'channel' / 'group' scoping

rules.rationale: Apr 28 2026 incident — bot auto-replied with the literal phrase context

Apr 28 2026 incident — the literal pairing codes that went to Chana and Herschel were 8-char A-Z0-9 sent as the entire message body. This shape is deterministic enough to catch without false positives on normal short replies (which contain spaces or lowercase).

alert_on: any bot attempting to bind a personal_identities_quarantined identifier
any send matching ask_before_emitting.patterns that wasn't explicitly approved
any deny_bind kind being attempted (regardless of identity)
